changes.before: Breakfast at Brennan’s has always been a long, celebratory meal, and the baked apple is a gentle start. The apple is baked until soft, with a crumble of oatmeal, pecans and raisins, then glazed with brown sugar. Sweetened crème fraîche — a slightly tangy cultured cream — balances the sweetness. It’s warm and comforting, and it comes after your Brandy Milk Punch eye opener, before the soup.

changes.before: New Orleans “barbecue” isn’t a smoker or a tomato sauce — it’s the buttery, peppery style made famous by barbecue shrimp. Here it’s lobster, which is sweet and rich. It sits on a white bean stew with ’nduja — en-DOO-yah — a spreadable, spicy pork sausage from Calabria in southern Italy, which melts into the beans and gives them a warm, red-pepper heat. Rich, spicy and comforting. We pour a Mâcon Chardonnay from Burgundy with it.

It’s rich and peppery, a real New Orleans flavor, and great to share before your eggs.

changes.before: Grand Isle is a barrier island on Louisiana’s coast, and these oysters are named for it. We serve them raw, very simply, so you taste the oyster: clean, briny and cold. A mignonette is the classic raw bar sauce, vinegar, shallot and cracked pepper, and ours is made with preserved Fresno chili, so it’s tangy with just a gentle warmth. Parsley adds a green note. They open our dinner tasting, too — a perfect first bite with Champagne.

TABLESIDE SAFETY: (1) Set the cart where nothing hangs overhead and away from drapes, décor and air vents; clear menus, napkins and paper from it. (2) Guests seated and back from the cart; no one leaning in; watch children, loose sleeves and long hair. (3) Measure the rum into a small vessel first — never pour from the bottle near a flame. (4) Pull the pan off the flame to add rum, then tilt the far edge toward the flame to ignite, away from you and the guests. (5) Never add alcohol to a lit pan. (6) Keep a lid or cover within reach to smother, and know where the extinguisher is. (7) Let the flame burn out before plating; turn the burner off before you leave the cart. Flambéing doesn’t remove all the alcohol — tell guests who avoid it. Dairy (butter, ice cream); ice cream likely contains egg. On the breakfast tasting it comes with Congregation Coffee & Chicory.
